questions.q: After browsing to and opening an Excel file, where do you land, just like every other connector?
options: Navigator
Model view
The Publish dialog
Power Query Editor, automatically
questions.explain: Every connector, Excel included, lands you in Navigator to choose what to load.

questions.q: Why might Power BI offer "Suggested Tables" for a single Excel sheet?
options: The file is a legacy .xls format
The workbook has more than one sheet
The sheet contains more than one distinct block of data, separated by blank rows/columns
Suggested Tables only appears for SQL sources, not Excel
questions.explain: When a sheet has multiple separate tables laid out with gaps between them, Power BI detects the pattern and offers each block as its own suggested table.

questions.q: What happens if you load the "whole sheet" instead of a suggested table, when a sheet has three separate data blocks?
options: Power BI refuses to load it and shows an error
Only the first block loads; the others are ignored
Power BI automatically merges the three blocks into one clean table
Every cell loads as one table, and the gaps between blocks become null values
questions.explain: The whole-sheet option loads every cell as-is, including the blank rows/columns between separate tables, which appear as null values.

questions.q: You notice 0.049 in Excel shows as 0.049000000000000002 in Power Query's preview. What's the best explanation?
options: Power Query has a bug and the value should be reported to Microsoft
The Excel file is corrupted
Excel itself can't store every decimal with perfect precision, and Power Query is showing the exact stored value
This only happens with legacy .xls files
questions.explain: This is a known, harmless quirk of binary floating-point storage in Excel — the underlying file already contains that longer value, and it doesn't affect calculations.

questions.q: What extra component do you need to connect to a legacy .xls or .xlsb workbook?
options: Nothing extra — legacy files work identically to .xlsx
The Access Database Engine OLEDB (ACE) provider
The Web connector
A Power BI Pro license
questions.explain: Legacy Excel formats require the ACE OLEDB provider to be installed; without it, Power BI shows an error naming the missing provider.
